title: The Day the Wind Took Attendance
skyStory: Forty-two percent of the moon is lit and it is holding onto Aquarius with both hands, because a proper November gale is barrelling in off the Atlantic. Aquarius is an air sign that rarely gets to show off like this. It is taking attendance: every loose leaf, every flapping bin lid, every brave umbrella. Everyone is accounted for. Several are now in a different town.

reading: The wind will rattle the cabin windows today and you will feel the urge to brace against everything at once. Don't. Cabins have stood through worse gales than this one by doing one thing: staying put and keeping the fire lit. Pick the thing that matters most and stand behind it.

Someone will come to you with a problem shaped like a tangled kite string. You will want to grab it and untangle the whole thing yourself, in public, at speed. Instead, hold one end and let them work the knots. Life Path 3 is the teacher, and the best teachers know when to hand the string back.
joel.mission: Step outside for one full minute in the wind, arms out like a kite, and shout one thing you are proud of.
joel.omen: A bin lid cartwheeling down the road. Chaos is happening, but none of it is yours to chase.
joel.stoneWhy: anchor stone for a windy day

reading: Gale day on the shore. The waves are showing off, throwing spray over the rocks like confetti at a very dramatic wedding. You are the rock, of course. Steady, unbothered, faintly amused, getting a little wet and not minding.

Courage today looks quiet. It looks like saying the one honest sentence in a meeting that everyone else is thinking. It looks like asking the question you assumed was obvious. The [[Strength]] card is not a lion-wrestler today; it is a hand resting gently on a lion's head while the wind howls. That is you. Hand gestures optional, but encouraged.
nancy.mission: Say the honest sentence before 3 pm, then reward yourself with something warm in a mug.
nancy.omen: A gull hovering perfectly still in a gale, going nowhere on purpose. Holding your position is progress.
nancy.stoneWhy: sea stone for a sea storm
nancy.elementWhy: the waves are on your side

together.text: Each of you tell the other one brave thing you did today, no matter how small. Answering an email you were dodging counts. Wearing the bright scarf counts. The wind is taking attendance, and it marks you both present with a gold star.
